name: CTLA-4 Haploinsufficiency

criteria.description: Heterozygous pathogenic mutation in the CTLA4 gene
Presence of autoimmune manifestations such as autoimmune cytopenias or endocrinopathies
Evidence of lymphoproliferation including lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, or granulomatous inflammation
Reduced CTLA-4 protein expression or function on regulatory T cells
Family history of immune dysregulation or CTLA-4 related disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a heterozygous pathogenic CTLA4 mutation plus at least two major clinical features (autoimmunity and/or lymphoproliferation)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by functional assays demonstrating CTLA-4 haploinsufficiency and exclusion of other immune dysregulation syndromes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Autoimmune cytopenias (e.g., autoimmune hemolytic anemia, immune thrombocytopenia)
Lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly due to lymphoproliferation

common.symptomName: Autoimmune endocrinopathies (e.g., thyroiditis, type 1 diabetes mellitus)
Chronic diarrhea due to autoimmune enteropathy
Eczema or other dermatological autoimmune manifestations

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms including headaches or peripheral neuropathy

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms including anxiety or depression

laboratory: Hypogammaglobulinemia with low IgG, IgA, and/or IgM
Presence of autoantibodies (e.g., ANA, anti-thyroid antibodies)
imaging: Lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly on ultrasound or CT
Interstitial lung disease on chest CT
Granulomatous lesions on imaging of affected organs
genetic: Heterozygous pathogenic variants in CTLA4 gene confirmed by sequencing
Reduced CTLA-4 protein expression/function on flow cytometry or functional assays
other: Histopathology showing lymphocytic infiltration or granulomas

distinguishingFeatures: LRBA deficiency shows similar immune dysregulation but caused by LRBA gene mutations
More prominent hypogammaglobulinemia and severe enteropathy
Often earlier onset and more severe infections
IPEX syndrome caused by FOXP3 mutations
Severe early-onset autoimmunity with enteropathy and endocrinopathy

redFlags: Severe, recurrent autoimmune cytopenias resistant to standard therapies
Early onset lymphoproliferation with splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy
Recurrent or severe infections with hypogammaglobulinemia
references: Schubert D, et al. Autosomal dominant immune dysregulation syndrome in humans with CTLA4 mutations. Nat Med. 2014;20(12):1410-1416.
Kuehn HS, et al. Immune dysregulation in human subjects with heterozygous germline mutations in CTLA4. Science. 2014;345(6204):1623-1627.
